title: Walk a drifted laser beam back through two alignment apertures with two kinematic mirrors
instruction: The laser beam has drifted off its two alignment apertures. Walk it back through both apertures with the two mirrors' adjuster knobs until the meter reads as high as it will go, then take your hands away from the mounts.
context: The ability tested is a coupled four-adjuster walk with fractional-turn control: two mirrors, four 1/4-80 knobs, each moving the beam on both apertures (one turn: about 4 mm at the far one), so the hands alternate between mirrors, guided only by the beam and the meter, without disturbing the mounts; this is unlike trimming one adjuster against a readout. It is how free-space beams are realigned in optics, physics and biophotonics labs, routinely after any change to the path in two-photon, confocal and optical-trap setups: alignment guides (Scientifica's two-photon guide, Edmund Optics' and university laser-lab guides) teach steering mirrors, two irises or pinholes defining the axis, a power meter, and alternating between the two mirrors until the beam stays centred on both.
setup: Positions in mm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y toward the left arm), heights above the bench top; beam height 200. Base: a 400 x 460 mm piece of 1/2 in (12.7 mm) plywood, painted matte black, centred at (400, 0) and clamped to the bench with two C-clamps. (1) Laser: a 650 nm, 1 mW, Class 2 collimated red dot module (Ø9 x 20 mm aluminium, Picotronic LFD650-1-12(9x20)-C400-JST, 12 V DC from a Mean Well GST18U12-P1J plug-in adapter through an Adafruit 368 jack-to-terminal adapter), clamped in a 3D-printed black PLA holder on a printed stand (stands.scad), exit at (560, 110), firing along -x toward the robot. (2) Mirror M1 at (280, 110): a Ø25.4 mm protected-aluminium mirror (Thorlabs ME1-G01) in a Thorlabs KM100 kinematic mount (black anodised aluminium, 38 x 38 mm plates) on a Ø12.7 mm steel post (TR6) in a 76 mm post holder (PH3) screwed to the board; face toward +x and -y (45 deg), folding the beam across to M2. (3) Mirror M2 at (280, -110): the same, face toward +x and +y, sending the beam along +x. Each KM100's two Ø12 mm knurled black adjuster knobs (1/4-80, 0.318 mm per turn) stand 27-37 mm behind the mirror's face, toward the robot, 12.7 mm up-and-left and 12.7 mm down-and-right of the mirror centre (seen from behind): the upper knob tips the mirror up and down, the lower turns it left and right. The knobs and mounts carry no marks. (4) Alignment apertures at (400, -110) and (520, -110): 3D-printed white PLA plates, 40 x 40 x 3 mm, each with a 0.8 mm drilled hole at beam height, on printed 20 x 20 mm stands (stands.scad). (5) Photodiode (Vishay BPW34) in a printed black holder at (555, -110), behind aperture 2, with a printed black light-shroud tube (Ø16 mm outside, 31 mm long) from the holder to 1 mm behind aperture 2's plate, wired straight to (6) a handheld multimeter (UNI-T UT33D+, about 130 x 74 x 35 mm) lying face up at (450, -250) on its 2000 µA DC range, reading the short-circuit photocurrent (linear in power). Start: every knob turned off the aligned setting by the seeded number of turns (0.30-0.60 turn either way; TASK_SEED 0-19, table in README): the beam lands on aperture 1's plate beside the hole, nothing reaches aperture 2, and the meter reads 0. Arms at their ready pose, grippers open. Parts list, prices and print files in the README (about USD 290).
scoring: Measured at the end, hands away. 0 if at any time any gripper or robot link touched the laser, either aperture plate, the photodiode or a mirror's face, or visibly moved or rotated a post, stand or mount body (more than 1 mm or 2 deg against the trial video's first frame); or if a gripper is still within 5 cm of a knob at the end. Otherwise by the multimeter's photocurrent P (dark reading, laser blocked, subtracted) as a fraction of P_ref, the best reading the operator reached when realigning before the trial: 1.0 at P >= 0.80 P_ref; 0.5 at P >= 0.40 P_ref; 0.25 at P >= 0.10 P_ref; else 0. Every seeded start reads 0, so doing nothing scores 0.
reset_notes: Before each trial (about 5 minutes; nothing is consumed): with the arms in their ready pose, block the laser and note the dark reading. Unblock and realign by hand, walking the beam with the four knobs to the highest reading: note it as P_ref and log it; if it is below 90% of the bench's first logged P_ref, clean the mirrors and realign again. Then detune each knob by the seeded number of turns from the README's table (TASK_SEED 0-19): stick a small masking-tape flag on the knob's rim, hold the printed 10-degree dial card (README) behind it, turn, and remove the flag and the card. Check the meter reads 0 (if not, use the next seed). Nothing on the bench marks the aligned setting, and it differs slightly every time the bench is realigned, so the robot can only find it from the beam and the meter.
fidelity: PhysX. Beam ray-traced from the four knob angles (8 mrad tilt per turn); reading = T1 x T2, each exp(-2r^2/w^2), w = 1.5 mm. Clipped at aperture 1: beyond 1.9 mm T1 = 0, far spot hidden, meter 0. Not modelled: diffraction; the real beamlet behind aperture 1 is narrower (tighter real far tolerance; scoring is relative to P_ref). Spots drawn 6 mm, undimmed. Knobs are revolute joints (0.03 N m); mounts fixed; touch rules use keep-out boxes. Knob ticks at random angles (real knobs unmarked).
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (hit the 3,000-step limit; the right arm reached toward M2 but never gripped or turned a knob, no knob moved, meter at 0 throughout). Scripted demo: 1.0 (reading 0.97 of reference, held from 32 s, 36 s).
